This article holds graphic pictures, each folded until pressed.

Summary

At least 60 vehicles were in the column when it was hit near the Wadi Sahm junction, at 15.4127, 44.2381 (plus code 7HXQ8C2X+3G), on 24 October 2025. We identify 14 of them by type, and at least 9 were destroyed or abandoned. Our confidence in the place is 90%, in the day 75%. @sahm_watch[1] posted the video[2] the same evening; the local news site[3] reported it the next day.

Limits. The count is a minimum: the footage shows the head of the column only. Two trucks (V07 and V11) may be one seen twice. Nothing here says who fired.

The footage

The first strike lands at [0:01–0:04], and the lead tank stops at [0:09].

Where it happened

The column was hit where the Sana'a road meets the wadi track, 1.2 km east of the bridge.

  • 15.412700, 44.238100 The junction
  • 15.413060, 44.236870 Rooftop (where it was filmed)

The junction before and after the ambush
Imagery: Esri Wayback, 12 March 2025 · Esri World Imagery, about 26 October 2025 [8]

The register

V12 is the clearest: the frame at [0:09] and a phone photo[12] show the same turret ring. We saw 12 trucks in the second frame.

Confirmed. The junction matches the frame: the road bend, the wadi track and the two compounds.

Unverified. V07 and V11 may be the same truck seen from two sides.

The phone photo

How it unfolded

Read from the ridge, the ambush took under a minute.

The column comes round the bend in close order, tanks first.

By the next morning the wrecks have been pushed off the road.
